findings.rationale: Migration output is computed from an earlier read, but the commit path checks only current file type and never verifies that contents still match the planned source. A concurrent edit between planning and rename is silently overwritten.

After a partial commit failure, restoration errors are ignored and every backup is then deleted. If a restore rename fails, the command returns an error after leaving some files migrated and discarding the recovery copy, violating the advertised batch atomicity.

The domain contract requires an idempotency key for irreversible effects, but replay scopes pending/completed operations only by effect name and correlation ID. Repeated requests with the same declared idempotency key but different correlations evade duplicate-commit detection; duplicate requests with the same correlation are also silently collapsed by BTreeSet::insert.

Generation writes files directly into an existing output tree one at a time. A failure leaves a mixed partial tree, and rerunning after the model removes or renames generated files leaves obsolete files behind, so the directory no longer represents the returned scaffold.

The evaluator compares current specification, artifact, generator, claim-set, and reviewed-document digests, but the CLI returns nonzero only when status is exactly signature-invalid. Other negative or stale evaluation states therefore produce a successful process exit and cannot reliably gate CI.
